subject: Post-call recap: BrightWorks trial — integration timeline, owners, and success criteria
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@brightworks.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightworks.io
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Redwood trial — integration plan & success metrics

Thanks for the demo this morning — quick recap from our side and next steps so we all have the same expectations.

Notes from call:
- Primary goal: evaluate Redwood for customer-facing summarization pipeline (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Success criteria (what BrightWorks needs to validate during the POC):
  * 95th percentile generation latency below 400ms for single-turn summary requests
  * Throughput of ~120 qps sustained for 30m bursts using a single reserved pool
  * Output quality: ROUGE-L parity within 5 points of current model baseline on 500-sample prompt set
  * No PII leakage for specified test corpus (we will provide examples)
- Integration requirements: SDK integration into our Java service, streaming token output to web clients, and tool-calling support to hit the external knowledge API.

We attached our trial requirements workbook (brightworks_trial_requirements.xlsx) — this includes sample prompts, latency profiles, and the procurement contact.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you propose an implementation timeline with named owners? Ideally a 3-week technical ramp + 2-week validation window.
2) Confirm which Redwood API routes we should use for streaming + tool-calling and any SDK version pins.
3) Share any security artifacts we need to triage (SOC2 / data handling) — procurement wants those to start the compliance review.

Alex
Director, ML Engineering
BrightWorks

---
Attachment: brightworks_trial_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 98KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@brightworks.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightworks.io
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood trial — integration plan & success metrics

Thanks Alex — appreciated the clear requirements. High level plan and owner assignments below. I kept this at a week-by-week cadence to match your suggested 3+2 window.

Summary timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): Paperwork + security handoff
  * Owner: Olga Petrov (setup procurement loop, share security docs)
  * Deliverables: NDA/POC MSA, redwood-security-questions.pdf (SOC2 summary + data handling brief)
- Week 1-3: Implementation & integration
  * Owner: Karthik Iyer (technical lead)
  * Activities: SDK embed in Java service, implement streaming endpoint, configure dedicated pool and quantization profile for latency targets
  * Deliverables: staging integration, sample load test script, instrumentation dashboard link
- Week 4-5: Validation & quality check
  * Owner: Marcus Lin (onboarding / eval lead)
  * Activities: run 500-sample prompt set, generate ROUGE & latency reports, security traces for sample corpus, go/no-go review

Answers to your asks: 
1) Implementation timeline and owners: see above — we can compress to 2 weeks of integration if BrightWorks can provide a dev environment and the Java service repo access on day 1.
2) API & SDK: Use the Redwood Java SDK v1.4.2 for initial integration (SDK routes: /v1/chat/streams for streaming, /v1/generate for non-streaming test harness). For tool-calling, enable function schema in the SDK and route external calls through our tool-proxy (tool-proxy.redwood.ai/execute) — Karthik will share a short example.
3) Security artifacts: attaching the SOC2 summary and a short data handling note. Procurement should get these this morning.

Quick clarifying Qs:
- Alex: can you confirm the identity of the external knowledge API (tool-calling target) and whether it requires client certs?
- Also confirm the sample corpus size and a point of contact for test data transfer.

I'll drop these into HubSpot and link the Drive folder once procurement confirms.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@brightworks.io>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightworks.io
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood trial — integration plan & success metrics

Alex — quick technical follow-up and concrete examples so your engineers can start integrating tomorrow.

SDK + routes (practical copy/paste):
- Java SDK (v1.4.2) snippet for streaming:
  /*
   * RedwoodStreamingClient client = RedwoodStreamingClient.builder().apiKey("<REDACTED>").build();
   * client.streamChat("model-redwood-8k", userPrompt, event -> handleToken(event));
   */
- API endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/streams (streaming), POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (batch tests)
- Tool-calling: define functions in the chat payload per the SDK docs; tool-proxy endpoint: https://tool-proxy.redwood.ai/execute. Use signed JWT from your service to call tool-proxy.

Performance knobs we'll configure for the trial:
- Dedicated pool with 2x A100-equivalent vGPUs for burst headroom
- Quantization profile: int8-fast (tradeoff test — we will run baseline vs int8-fast)
- Continuous batching disabled for latency-critical paths; set max_batch_delay_ms=12

Streaming behavior notes (important):
- Streaming will emit token deltas with incremental latency ~15-30ms per token. For short summaries we expect end-to-end <400ms when the model is pinned and KV cache warmed.
- If your front-end needs char-level streaming, we'll provide a simple JS wrapper that converts token deltas to pseudo-chunks.

I'll upload a minimal example repo to the Drive folder and paste links in HubSpot. Marcus — could you schedule the load window for Week 3 (preferably Tue morning PST)?

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: (code sample) redwood-java-streaming-example.zip (archive, 12KB)

- BrightWorks will provide dev repo access and sample corpus by EOD Monday (we aim for Week 1 start on Nov 23).
- External knowledge API is called FactsAPI (facts-api.brightworks.io) and it uses a token header — no client certs. We'll share API keys for the tool-proxy flow.
- Procurement has the SOC2 summary; they'll ping when they complete the initial review.

Two asks before we kick off: 
1) Can Marcus share the load test script and instrumentation dashboard link?
2) Short 30-min technical alignment call with Karthik + our SRE on Monday (Nov 22) at 10am PST to run through the streaming example and auth for tool-proxy.

If you can confirm both items here, we'll formalize the PO and calendar invites.
